title: Rigveda 10.47: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.47: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.47 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 2v-3v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.47.1 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 2v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ja̱gṛ̱bhmā te̱ dakṣi̍ṇam indra̱ hasta̍ṁ vasū̱yavo̍ vasupate̱ vasū̍nām | vi̱dmā hi tvā̱ gopa̍tiṁ śūra̱ gonā̍m a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>THY right hand have we grasped in ours, O Indra, longing for treasure, Treasure-Lord of treasures! Because we know thee, Hero, Lord of cattle: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 2v (OPenn image 2, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.46.8 ‹pāvakam mandraṁ hotāraṁ dadhire›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 3r, begins in RV 10.47.2 ‹-carkṛtyaṁ śaṁsyam bhūrivāram asmabhyaṁ›. Verse 10.47.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.47.2-6 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 3r
translation.original_text:
2svā̱yu̱dhaṁ svava̍saṁ sunī̱thaṁ catu̍ḥsamudraṁ dha̱ruṇa̍ṁ rayī̱ṇām | ca̱rkṛtya̱ṁ śaṁsya̱m bhūri̍vāram a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
3su̱brahmā̍ṇaṁ de̱vava̍ntam bṛ̱hanta̍m u̱ruṁ ga̍bhī̱ram pṛ̱thubu̍dhnam indra | śru̱taṛ̍ṣim u̱gram a̍bhimāti̱ṣāha̍m a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
4sa̱nadvā̍ja̱ṁ vipra̍vīra̱ṁ taru̍traṁ dhana̱spṛta̍ṁ śūśu̱vāṁsa̍ṁ su̱dakṣa̍m | da̱syu̱hana̍m pū̱rbhida̍m indra sa̱tyam a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
5aśvā̍vantaṁ ra̱thina̍ṁ vī̱rava̍ntaṁ saha̱sriṇa̍ṁ śa̱tina̱ṁ vāja̍m indra | bha̱dravrā̍ta̱ṁ vipra̍vīraṁ sva̱rṣām a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
6pra sa̱ptagu̍m ṛ̱tadhī̍tiṁ sume̱dhām bṛha̱spati̍m ma̱tir acchā̍ jigāti | ya ā̍ṅgira̱so nama̍sopa̱sadyo̱ 'smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
2Wealth, fully armed, good guard and kind protector, sprung from four seas, the prop and stay of treasures, Fraught with great bounties, meet for praise and glory; vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
3Wealth, with good Brahmans, Indra! God-attended, high, wide, and deep, arid based on broad foundations, Strong, with famed R̥ishis, conquering our foemen: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
4Victorious, winning strength, with hero sages, confirmed in power, most useful, wealth-attracting, True, Indra! crushing forts and slaying Dasyus: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
5Wealthy in heroes and in cars and horses, strength hundredfold and thousandfold, O Indra, With manly sages, happy troops, Iight-winning: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
6To Saptagu the sage, the holy-minded, to him, Br̥ihaspati, the song approaches, Angiras' Son who must be met with homage: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 3r (OPenn image 2, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.47.2 ‹-carkṛtyaṁ śaṁsyam bhūrivāram asmabhyaṁ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 3v, begins in RV 10.47.7 ‹-hṛdispṛśo manasā vacyamānā asmabhyaṁ›. Verses 10.47.2-6 end on this page; 10.47.2 begins on fol. 2v.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.47.7-8 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 4); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 3v
translation.original_text:
7vanī̍vāno̱ mama̍ dū̱tāsa̱ indra̱ṁ stomā̍ś caranti suma̱tīr i̍yā̱nāḥ | hṛ̱di̱spṛśo̱ mana̍sā va̱cyamā̍nā a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
8yat tvā̱ yāmi̍ da̱ddhi tan na̍ indra bṛ̱hanta̱ṁ kṣaya̱m asa̍ma̱ṁ janā̍nām | a̱bhi tad dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī gṛ̍ṇītām a̱smabhya̍ṁ ci̱traṁ vṛṣa̍ṇaṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
7My lauds, like envoys, craving loving-kindness, go forth to Indra with their strong entreaty, Moving his heart and uttered by my spirit: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
8Grant us the boon for which I pray, O Indra, a spacious home unmatched among the people. To this may Heaven and Earth accord approval: vouchsafe us mighty and resplendent riches.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 3v (OPenn image 3, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.47.7 ‹-hṛdispṛśo manasā vacyamānā asmabhyaṁ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 4r, begins in RV 10.48.3 ‹-mām āryanti kṛtena kartvena›. Verses 10.47.7-8 end on this page; 10.47.7 begins on fol. 3r.
